property_summary: The supportsInterface function should return true when queried with the IERC1155 interface id.
After calling adjustAdminAccess on an unknown caller, the supportsInterface return for IERC1155 interface id is unchanged.
The supportsInterface function must return true for the IERC1155 interface id when queried from any address.
The contract's supportsInterface returns true when queried with the IERC1155 interface id, regardless of prior admin access adjustments.
adjustAdminAccess should not change the return value of supportsInterface for an arbitrary interface id.

For any interface ID, after calling adjustAdminAccess, the supportsInterface function returns the same value as the original contract's ERC165 supportsInterface if the ID is not IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI.
The supportsInterface function returns true for the IERC165 interface ID (0x01ffc9a7).
The supportsInterface function returns false for the ERC1155 interface ID (0xd9b67a26) when it should return true.
Calling supportsInterface with a random bytes4 input always returns the same value on P and M after adjusting admin access.
After adjusting admin access, supportsInterface always returns true for the IERC165 interface ID (0x01ffc9a7) on the reference contract.
balanceOf returns 0 for the zero address when the account parameter is address(0)
For the zero address, balanceOf returns 0 in the correct reference and returns the stored non-zero balance in the buggy version.
The balanceOf function returns the same value for address(0) as for any other account with the same id.
balanceOf does not revert when called with address(0) and any token id; the reference reverts while the buggy version does not.
balanceOf returns 0 for the zero address when the id is 0.
balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length equals accounts.length for any input arrays.

balanceOfBatch returns consistent lengths for accounts and ids arrays that are passed directly to the function without reordering, ensuring that the returned array length matches accounts.length when ids.length equals accounts.length.
For any input arrays, the length of the returned array from balanceOfBatch equals the length of the accounts array.
balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length always equals the length of the accounts parameter.
balanceOfBatch returns an array whose i-th element matches balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) for every valid i.

The balanceOfBatch function returns an array with the same length as the accounts array, even when accounts and ids arrays have different lengths (which would cause a revert due to the require statement).
The returned array length from balanceOfBatch must equal the length of the accounts array.
The lengths of accounts and ids arrays must be equal for balanceOfBatch to succeed.
The balanceOfBatch function succeeds (does not revert) when input arrays have equal length.
The balanceOfBatch function should return an array of the correct length (equal to accounts.length) when accounts and ids have equal length, and should revert when they have different lengths.
balanceOfBatch should not revert when called with valid arrays of equal length by an EOA without any role.
balanceOfBatch always returns an array with length equal to accounts.length.
After adjustAdminAccess is called, the daily allowance replenish time for any address and tokenId is never set to a timestamp in the past (i.e., less than block.timestamp).
After calling adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for any address and tokenId never decreases without a corresponding replenish time update.
After adjustAdminAccess is called, the daily allowance replenish time for any address and tokenId never equals the current block.timestamp (it should be strictly greater than block.timestamp).
After adjustAdminAccess returns, dailyAllowanceReplenishTime for any address and tokenId is never less than or equal to block.timestamp.
After adjustAdminAccess is called, the daily allowance replenish time for any address and tokenId is never set to a timestamp that is not strictly greater than block.timestamp.
After adjusting admin access, the allowance remaining for a token owner on a token ID should be equal to the result of the public getter getAllowanceRemaining for that owner and token ID.
After calling adjustAdminAccess(address,bool), the replenish time should be greater than 0 if allowance is being replenished.

After calling adjustAdminAccess with any arguments, the allowanceRemaining for any owner and token ID that is not stored as a transient state should be less than or equal to the dailyAllowance of that token.

After any successful call to adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for any address and any token ID should be at most the dailyAllowance of that token if the dailyAllowanceReplenishTime for that address and token ID is in the past.

After a call to adjustAdminAccess that sets an address as admin, getAllowanceRemaining for any owner and token ID should be equal to that token's dailyAllowance if the current time is after the replenish time.

After adjustAdminAccess completes, the allowanceRemaining for any (user, tokenId) pair is consistent with the dailyAllowanceReplenishTime: if the replenish time has passed, the allowance equals the dailyAllowance, otherwise it holds the stored value.

After adjustAdminAccess completes, for any (user, tokenId) pair, if dailyAllowanceReplenishTime[user][tokenId] <= block.timestamp, then allowanceRemaining[user][tokenId] equals allGameItemAttributes[tokenId].dailyAllowance.

After adjustAdminAccess, the dailyAllowanceReplenishTime for any caller and tokenId is either zero or greater than the current block timestamp, because if the replenish time is ever set, the mutant fails to set it, leaving it at default zero.
After adjustAdminAccess completes, the allowanceRemaining for a user and tokenId is at most the dailyAllowance defined in the game item attributes.
After any public entry point that ends with adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for a user and tokenId never exceeds the dailyAllowance defined for that token.
After adjusting admin access for any address, the allowanceRemaining for that address for any tokenId is not less than the previous value.
After any call to adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining at the keys used in any previous mint call remains unchanged (equal to the value set during the last replenishment).
After the first mint for a user-token pair that triggers replenishment (dailyAllowanceReplenishTime ≤ block.timestamp), the allowanceRemaining equals the dailyAllowance of that token.
After any adjustable admin access, the allowanceRemaining for the caller and any tokenId that has been replenished remains equal to the dailyAllowance of that token.
After adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining for any address and any tokenId is always ≤ token's daily allowance.
After any call to adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for any user and token remains exactly the dailyAllowance (or zero if dailyAllowance was not set).
After adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining for any token with dailyAllowance > 0 does not exceed its dailyAllowance nor equal the maximum uint256.
After any call to adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining for the caller and any token never exceeds the token's dailyAllowance plus the difference between previous allowance and dailyAllowance.
After adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining for any address and token is strictly less than type(uint256).max, because the reference only sets it to dailyAllowance which is finite.
After any call to adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining for any address and any token is always less than type(uint256).max.

For any identical pair of calls (admin1, admin2, access1, access2), if adjustAdminAccess(admin1, access1) followed by adjustAdminAccess(admin2, access2) is called, the allowanceRemaining entries of the caller for any token never increase after the second call.
The allowanceRemaining value for the caller after minting is always between 0 and the dailyAllowance of the token.
After adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for any account and token id is unchanged from before the call.
After any number of adjustAdminAccess calls, the allowanceRemaining for any address and token ID never increases for the caller.
After any call to adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for a fixed address and token that never interacted with adjustAdminAccess remains unchanged.
